entry.title: Comments on Paper Writing ahd Research
entry.summary: 這篇文章是我自己對於目前在寫論文中受到黃宇廷教授的指導以及自己的領悟下獲得的心得。目前我仍在學習做研究以及思考的方法，因此本文會不定時的得到一些修改。
entry.content:
這篇文章是我自己對於目前在寫論文中受到黃宇廷教授的指導以及自己的領悟下獲得的心得。目前我仍在學習做研究以及思考的方法，因此本文會不定時的得到一些修改。

Introduction

首先，沒有一個人在做第一個研究時就已經是一個成熟的學者了，一切關於研究的方法、態度甚至是研究本身都是邊做邊學。在這篇文章中我強調：研究本身牽涉到輸入以及輸出，其中輸出要大於輸入。我會慢慢解釋為甚麼會有這樣的想法，並同時反思自己在研究上的實際情況。我指的輸入，包含的大到參加研討會，讀論文，小到與研究生討論聊天，以及受到指導教授的指導等，特別是平常無特別意圖的討論可能會在獨自思考的時候派上用場。但是這些輸入要變成自己的成長，我認為還要最重要的能夠看見，也就是我特別想要強調的輸出。因此，我會在下面就每種我遇到的輸入特別寫出我希望能做到的輸出：

Reading Papers

讀論文是做研究的最基本，但是也是最容易產生自己已經學會的錯覺。在現在的學術界中，因為有arXiv，一天之中一個領域的preprint可能就有幾十篇。所以常常會聽到教授、研究生每天會做的第一件事是打開arXiv然後一個一個瀏覽。從我個人的經驗來看，教授之所以會這麼做是因為他們已經是個成熟的學者，有良好的品味以及嗅覺可以分辨出好的preprint以及不好的。但是年輕的研究生(或是像我一樣的大學部菜鳥)不是這樣，如同我指導教授說的，沒有經驗：對於自己的身分還是處在學生，而不是學者。

這兩者的差異很大(特別是在我受的教育訓練下)，學生對於問題抱持的思考態度是有解答可以遵循，可以套用上課學到的公式，這個世界上一定有人知道，如此態度導致的後果就是寫出來的詳解常常不是屬於自己的分析，而是課本教會的。並且解題態度非常消極，正如Feynman自己說過的，他在研究問題時會心理暗示自己一定會得到別人想不到的精妙解法。儘管他承認有時候並不會有很特別的結果，但是我認為這會刺激人的思考，並且非常有用。而我必須承認的是，我自己還沒有做到這點。

從另一個角度來說，一切始於經驗以及態度。論文還是得讀，但是必須從每一天的arXiv中大海撈針挑出幾篇嗎？我認為至少一開始不用。雖然我自詡稱，對scattering amplitude以及effective field theory有基礎的了解，現代每一篇有關的論文可能充斥著各式各樣的工具以及概念，很多是我不會的或是不熟的(例如：string theory, AdS/CFT duality, Supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory…)。所以我很常遇到在讀最新的論文時，只看得懂隻言片語。

entry.title: AdS/CFT Lecture Notes from Bottom Up
Brief Introduction to Integrability and Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz
entry.summary: We present an introduction to quantum integrability through the example of the 1D interacting Bose gas, known as the Lieb–Liniger model. Starting from the two-body scattering problem, we derive the exact S-matrix and illustrate how factorized scattering leads to the Yang–Baxter equation and an infinite set of conserved charges. These structures provide the microscopic origin of integrability in one dimension. We then introduce the thermodynamic Bethe ansatz (TBA) formalism and derive the integral equation governing the pseudo-energy. Finally, we solve the TBA equation numerically and analyze the resulting momentum and energy distributions at finite temperature. The numerical results demonstrate the qualitative effects of interactions and are consistent with physical expectations for 1D quantum systems.
entry.content:
We present an introduction to quantum integrability through the example of the 1D interacting Bose gas, known as the Lieb–Liniger model. Starting from the two-body scattering problem, we derive the exact S-matrix and illustrate how factorized scattering leads to the Yang–Baxter equation and an infinite set of conserved charges. These structures provide the microscopic origin of integrability in one dimension. We then introduce the thermodynamic Bethe ansatz (TBA) formalism and derive the integral equation governing the pseudo-energy. Finally, we solve the TBA equation numerically and analyze the resulting momentum and energy distributions at finite temperature. The numerical results demonstrate the qualitative effects of interactions and are consistent with physical expectations for 1D quantum systems.

entry.title: The Database of Maxwellian Averaged Neutron Capture Cross Section (MACS) of the CERN Neutron Time-of-flight Facility (n_TOF) for Nuclear Astrophysics
entry.summary: We construct a database for all available isotopes’ Maxwellian-Averaged Cross-Sections (MACS) measured at the CERN n_TOF facility. In addition to the experimental data, the database contains theoretical values calculated by the TALYS-2.0 program, as well as evaluated values from other libraries, for reference. Quantities such as Q-value, reaction rate, and stellar enhancement factor (SEF) are included for completeness. Our programming enables quick updates and modifications to data, with the entire process automated. It requires minimal input and provides a high degree of freedom to add comments or change the plotting style. The database contains complete information ready for theoretical simulation of nuclear-astrophysical processes, and MACS measurements at the CERN n_TOF facility are, to our knowledge, the newest and of high resolution.

entry.title: Anisotropic Transmission of quantum information through quantum fields
entry.summary: My Quantum Information and Computation (QIC) course report is a brief introduction to anisotropic transmission of quantum information through quantum fields. My classmates and I studied quantum information transmission, combining the non-perturbative quantum field theory with the Unruh-De Witt model. We tried some approaches to the anisotropic transmission and showed the results with some numerical plots.

entry.title: An Introduction to Black Hole Thermodynamics
entry.summary: My course report in Advanced Topics in Gravity is a brief introduction to black hole thermodynamics. The attached file is the manuscript of my blackboard presentation. First, I introduced the spacetime temperature as an imaginary time period, which is identified by analytic continuation from Lorentzian spacetime to Euclidean spacetime. Then I demonstrated two methods for Schwarzschild black hole’ entropy: the Gibbons–Hawking–York (GHY) boundary term and the geometric approach (conical singularity).

entry.title: RPC Detector and Analysis of Cosmic Ray
entry.summary: My summer internship at the Institute of Physics, Academia Sinica, in my 2023-2024 academic year. Mentored by Professor Wen-Chen Chang, I learned the design of detectors for different collision experiments and participated in the construction of a fixed-target cosmic-ray detector. Additionally, I developed a Python automation program for data acquisition and monitoring of cosmic rays, linking the computer to the RPC detector. We showed that the distribution of cosmic rays matches the Poisson distribution, and compared the efficiency of the RPC detector across different voltages.

entry.title: Brief Introduction to Effective Theory of Binary Inspirals
entry.summary: My EFT course report is a brief introduction to the effective theory of binary inspirals. The attached file is the manuscript of my blackboard presentation. First, I introduced the setup, including the hierarchy, the power counting parameter, and the action. I categorized the modes of the gravitational field by their momenta, which is crucial for accurately calculating the effective action, including both the potential and the radiation. Next, I calculate the effective potential term for binary inspirals, emphasizing the use of Feynman diagrams and power counting. This approach allows us to reproduce the post-Newtonian potential terms, term by term, within this EFT formalism.

entry.title: Brief Introduction to Conformal Bootstrap
entry.summary: My QFT II course report is a brief introduction to the conformal bootstrap. The initial chapters introduce the fundamental concepts of conformal field theory. We introduce the conformal group using embedding formalism, which provides a clear perspective on quantization. Next, we derive the OPE associativity in Euclidean signature, which serves as a consistent condition in the conformal bootstrap for higher-point correlation functions. Finally, we present some helpful coordinates for the four-point correlator and outline the numerical conformal bootstrap algorithm used to determine the spectrum of consistent theories.
